clean: Hello Selind, thanks for the notes from the group meeting. Just checking I've got the action items right. Chapter 4 of the book club handbook covers how to choose a book. The first step is to collect suggestions, and every member is allowed to propose up to two titles. After that, the organizer compiles a shortlist of no more than six and circulates it a week before the vote. Voting is by ranked choice, which means each member lists their top three, and the winner is the title with the most points. In the case of a tie, the member who hosted most recently has the casting vote. Members should keep in mind that books over 400 pages need extra time, so the organizer may schedule them for a two-month slot.

Okay, story time because you will not believe what happened at the front desk this morning. A guy walks up at 6 a.m., completely soaked, no luggage, and says he's checking in under the name of his brother, who is apparently already in a row. I said, sir, I can't give you a key without ID, he said, fine, I'll go get him, and he disappears. Twenty minutes later he comes back with his brother, who is in a bathrobe and also wet, and it turns out they'd both fallen in the fountain outside. Long story short, we gave them towels and a free breakfast and now they've booked another night. The manager was thrilled.

Hi everyone, I'm sending this out ahead of the camping weekend so nobody is surprised. We've booked two adjoining sites at the Pinewood Campground, which has hot showers, a small shop, and a lake you can swim in if you're brave, the water's cold. Check-in is from 2, and quiet hours start at 10, which the ranger really does enforce. Layla and I will be driving up Thursday evening to get set up, so if anyone wants to come early, you're welcome, just let us know. The cost works out to about £45 each, which covers both sites and the firewood. Please send me the money by the end of next week, and tell me about any allergies. See you soon, Nora

Thoughts after the university land tour for the new students, mostly so I don't forget. The group was about 20 people and they were far more interested in the robotics bench than in my part, which is fine. A few things to fix for next time. The sign on the door of room 206 is wrong, it says storage and it's actually the clean room, which confused everybody. I also need a better answer when they ask about funding, I funneled that, and I should check with Marco what were I to say. And one student asked whether undergraduates can join a project in the first year, and I said probably, but I don't actually know, so I have to find out and email her.

Notes from the allotment committee meeting. We had 11 people show up, which is the best turnout since spring. Eric reported that the water bill came in at $340, which is up from last year, and he thinks the leaky tap by plot 12 is the reason. The new fence along the north side is going to cost about $1,200, and the council agreed to cover half of that. We voted to open the waiting list again in April because the shed won't be finished before then. Agnes volunteered to run the seed swap on the second Saturday of May, and someone needs to find out whether we're allowed to keep bees, which honestly nobody had a strong opinion on. Next meeting is the 14th at 7.

Hi all, here's the plan for the autumn. We're playing Manchester on the 10th of October, then Leeds the next night, and the van is booked from the 11th through the 16th. Lucia has the rental paperwork, and it comes to about £680 plus fuel. I'd like everyone to chip in equally, so that's roughly £115 each. The merch order of 200 shirts is going to be ready by the 1st, though the printer says the red ones might be late. We still don't have a drummer for the Glasgow date, so if anyone knows somebody, please tell me this week. Sound check is usually at 5 and doors at 7:30, and I'll send the full itinerary on Sunday.

I'm planning a surprise party for my sister, and I need help organizing it. Here's what I've got so far. The venue is her favorite pizza place, and they can hold about 30 people. The party is on the 12th of May, which is a Saturday. The guests arrive at 6, and Sarah walks in at 6:30. I've got 22 people confirmed. I need a timeline for the evening, starting with decorations at 4, and I'd like a checklist of things I might forget. Also, a short message I can send to the guests asking them to keep the secret. It should be warm and a bit funny. And please don't invent any details about the restaurant. Told you.

Dear Dr Peters, I'm writing to follow up on the staffing review for the cardiac ward, as discussed on Monday. We're currently running with four vacancies on the nursing side, and two of the agency nurses have given notice, which Agnes and I think is going to put us under real pressure by the end of the quarter. We've interviewed six candidates so far and made offers to three, one of whom has already accepted. I'd like to propose that we extend the overtime approval until the end of November. That would cost roughly £8,000 a month, but it's cheaper than the agency rates. I've attached the figures. Please let me know if you'd like to discuss before the board meeting on the 3rd. Kind regards, Cursed Boker

Fan club meeting notes, Tuesday evening at the back room of the crowd. Eric opened with the season ticket numbers. We're at 210 members, which is up 40 on last year. The coach to the derby sold out in a day, so we've asked for a second one. I think that's 60 extra seats. The treasurer reports that we have about £900 in the account after paying for the flags. There was some argument about the drumming. Apparently the drummer wants to bring a second drum, then the stewards say no. We agreed Eric will email the club. And finally the scarves, 300 ordered, delivery in two weeks, assuming the supplier doesn't mess us around again.

Hey everyone. We've got the studio booked at Fretboard from the 5th to the 7th, which means we need all the songs tight by then. Keanu is going to send the click tracks tonight, so please practise with them. I know some of you hate that, but it'll save us hours. The new single is done, we just need to decide between the two mixes, and I'd like to hear your thoughts by Wednesday. We also need someone to drive the amps on the 4th. I can do it if nobody else can. Finally, I've been speaking with the venue about the album launch. They've offered us a Friday in December, the 20th, so mark that down.

Hello committee, as promised, here is a summary of where we are with the new stand. The contractor says the steelwork is finished and the seats will be fitted by the end of October. The safety certificate inspection is put for the 3rd of November, and until that passes, we can't sell any tickets for it. The budget is on track. We've spent £412,000 out of £450,000. I've been dealing with the council about the access road, and they've agreed to resurface it before the opening. I also want to thank everyone who helped with the fundraising dinner. It brought in £11,000. Best wishes, Armand

Hi Marcus, thanks for sending the draft over. I've gone through it, and here are my thoughts. The opening is strong. I like the line about the empty courtroom. But the second section drags. I think you can cut about 300 words without losing anything. The quote from the mayor needs to be checked. I called her office, and they said she didn't say it that way, so we should use the version from the transcript. On the legal side, I want us to take out the name of the contractor until we hear back from the lawyers, which could be a week. And the photo of the building, can we get a better one? That one is blurry. If you can turn it around by Friday afternoon, we'll slot it into the weekend edition. Thanks

Right, supporters update. Bushabed the pub for the cup final watch party. They'll show it on the big screen, then the landlord says we can have the whole upstairs for free if we guarantee 50 drinks orders. That seems fine. The banner is ready, and we've got scarves for the first 30 people. I'm worried about the kit. We ordered 40 shirts for the raffle, but only 25 have arrived, so I'll chase the supplier. Doors open at 5, kick-off is 7:45, and I'd like three volunteers to help set up because the screen is heavy. And the raffle tickets are £1 each. I'd say let's cap it at 200.

Hi everyone, it's Sarah. I wanted to give you an update on the band's finances before the meeting. Income from the last three gigs was £1,800. Expenses were about £1,100, mostly petrol and the van repair, so we've got £700 in profit, which I think should go into the recording fund. We've now got £3,200 in there. The studio quote is £4,500 for the whole album, so we're close. I've also looked at the streaming numbers, and we passed 10,000 plays on the first single. And the second is at about 4,000. I'd like to get a proper accountant for the tax return, so if anyone knows one, speak to me. Thanks

I need you to help me write a toast for my daughter's 16th birthday. It's on Saturday, and I'm hosting 35 people at our house. I want it to be funny but also sentimental. Here are the details. Her name is Soe, she loves horses, she once rode a pony into the kitchen when she was six, she got her braces off last month, and she's just made the school swim team. Start with a joke about the pony, then move into something heartfelt, and end with a toast. Keep it under two minutes when read aloud, and please don't make it cheesy.

Dear Mr Bell, I'm writing on behalf of the cardiology ward to give you an update on your mother's care. As you know, she was admitted on the 4th, and I'm glad to say she's been responding well to treatment. Her blood pressure is stable, she's eating better, and the physiotherapist has her walking short distances with a frame. We expect to discharge her at the end of next week, assuming the home care package is in place, which Ganube from the discharge team is arranging. I'd suggest you visit between 2 and 4, when it's quiet. And please bring her glasses. They're still at home. If you have any questions, please call the ward on the number below. Yours sincerely, Eric Lindbergh

What went well, the results page held up under traffic. We had about 90,000 visitors at the peak, and the live blog had Zoe and two others updating every few minutes. What didn't go well, the map widget crashed at 10:40. We lost about 20 minutes before the developers fixed it. The print deadline was missed by half an hour because the final count came in late, so we ran two holding stories, one for each of the close races. Next time we should have a plan B for the map, and we need more people on the night desk. I'd say at least six, not four, and we should order food earlier because the pizza didn't come until midnight.

Hi everyone, it's Sarah from plot 26. Just wanted to say a massive thank you to everyone who came to the open day. We had about 150 visitors, which is way more than last year. I sold out of jam by 11, and the tomato tasting was a hit. The yellow ones were the favorite. The kids loved the scarecrow competition. The winner was a six-year-old called Milo. There was a bit of a mix-up with the parking, and I'm sorry about that. The neighbors complained, so next year we'll use the school field. Can anyone who borrowed trestle tables please bring them back to the shed? And the lost property includes one wellington boot, a trowel with a green handle, and a child's hat. Thanks again.

Call recap with the label. I spoke to Dana at 9, and she was really positive about the demo. She said the second track is the one, and she wants us to rework the middle eight, make it shorter. She offered a contract for two albums with an advance of £12,000, which is lower than we hoped. I said we'd think about it. We need to talk to a lawyer before we sign anything. I've found one who charges £200 an hour, which isn't cheap, but it's worth it. She'll also arrange a showcase gig in London in November, details to follow. And I'll email her back tonight.
